html:
SMTO-FIL-0021 — That location is outside the folders SMTO may use

GUID: c92064a5-d2c7-4f9c-bec2-bde7571f00a6
Slug: file-path-outside-policy
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO may only work with files inside certain folders on the Gateway's computer. This location is outside them, or the request would delete or move a whole drive or SMTO's main work folder. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and look at the Working directory shown for this Gateway. If none is shown, the Gateway uses its own work folder. That folder is where SMTO is allowed to work, so it tells you where the files need to be.
  2. Put the files you want SMTO to use inside that folder, then tell SMTO their location there, without .. (meaning "the folder above"). Locations inside the folder pass the check; anything that climbs out of it is refused.
  3. If you asked SMTO to delete or move the whole working folder or a whole drive, ask for the specific files or subfolders instead. SMTO never deletes or moves a drive or its own work folder as a whole.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the step on files inside its allowed folder.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO really needs a folder outside its working folder, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they decide which folders it may use. Don't point a saved Run at a different computer or folder just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation was rejected by path containment: the resolved path escapes the guard root (the Gateway working directory) or the approved task file scope, targets deletion or move of a filesystem or guarded root, or a patch path is absolute or traverses outside its base.

What this means

  • Enabled containment/unsafe-action checks reject a path outside its root, a filesystem/root deletion or move, or a non-relative/traversing patch path. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Enabled containment/unsafe-action checks reject a path outside its root, a filesystem/root deletion or move, or a non-relative/traversing patch path.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare canonical operands with the accepted root and protected-root rules; symlink resolution is part of the check.

How to fix it

  • Compare path_context and the cwd fact with the guard root (execution_root, normally the Gateway's terminal_cwd). Use a path inside that root, an accepted artifact or temp root, or the task-approved scope. An administrator can change the root in Settings › Setup › Gateways or the per-user workspace_cwd_guard_enabled setting, but should not disable it as a routine fix (gateway_core/file_common.Operation.inside, file_manage.delete/move, file_patch.patch_path/patch).
  • Use a path within the authorized root or select the intended authorized target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation stays within authorized roots and does not target a protected root itself.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
